flashcards.front: Why do chat servers pair Cassandra with `(chat_id, bucket)` partition keys and Snowflake/seq clustering keys?
flashcards.back: LSM-tree storage handles massive write rates (hundreds of thousands of messages/sec), while partitioning by `(chat_id, month)` keeps single-conversation scroll queries sequential on one shard without unbounded partition growth.

quizzes.scenario: A chat gateway pod holding 100,000 WebSockets crashes. All 100,000 clients reconnect immediately and overload the auth and session tier.
quizzes.question: Which mitigation stops the reconnect storm?
options: Client backoff with full jitter plus edge connection shaping
Sticky routing so each client returns to its original pod
Larger session tokens so each reconnect skips the auth check
Client retries at a fixed 2-second delay to stay predictable
quizzes.explanation: Clients reconnecting on a fixed schedule arrive together. Exponential backoff with random (full) jitter spreads the reconnects over tens of seconds, and rate-shaping new connections at the edge protects the auth tier from whatever burst remains.
optionExplanations: Correct. Jitter spreads reconnects, and shaping caps the rest.
The original pod crashed, and stickiness does not slow the reconnects.
Skipping auth is a security change and does not spread the load.
A fixed delay makes every client retry at the same moment again.
